findings.title: Invalidate connected calendars after deleting the cache
findings.body: The delete-cache success handler only invokes an optional onSuccess callback; it never invalidates the connectedCalendars query. The wrapper forwards props.onChanged rather than refetching its query, and disables refetchOnWindowFocus. When no callback is supplied, deletion succeeds but the UI continues showing the deleted cache's timestamp and deletion action until a reload. Invalidate connectedCalendars here, as the disconnect mutation already does.

findings.title: Resolve backing cache records for in-memory delegated connections
findings.body: An in-memory delegated Google connection has a synthetic negative credential ID, but CalendarCacheRepository.getCachedAvailability can serve it from a real credential's cache using userId and the calendar key. Looking up status only by the synthetic ID always returns null. The connected-calendar helper also hides the matching nondelegated connection, so delegated users cannot inspect or clear cache that is actually serving their availability. Resolve the backing user-owned cache for these connections; the deletion handler must likewise support that ownership resolution rather than requiring the synthetic ID to exist in Credential.

findings.title: Explicitly write the selected-calendar refresh timestamp
findings.body: Passing an empty data object to Prisma updateMany does not advance @updatedAt; Prisma leaves that field unchanged for an empty update. Consequently, this new call does not update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt after a successful availability refresh, despite its stated purpose. Supply an explicit updatedAt value, or remove the call if selected-calendar refresh tracking is no longer needed.

findings.title: Resolve the environment file relative to the script location
findings.body: ENV_FILE is resolved relative to the caller's working directory. Running bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repository root therefore writes ../.env outside the repository, creating it if necessary, instead of updating the repository's environment file. The script reports success while the calendar service retains its previous webhook URL. Derive the environment-file path from the script's directory.

findings.title: Avoid the macOS-only sed invocation
findings.body: The separated empty argument in sed -i '' is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU sed, used on Linux, it is interpreted as an empty editing script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, so an existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is not replaced. The script still prints that the update succeeded, leaving webhook subscriptions pointed at the old tunnel. Use a portable replacement mechanism or handle BSD and GNU sed separately.
